Introduction

NELL is a South Korean alternative rock band known for their melancholic, dreamy sound. The band currently consists of lead vocalist, keyboardist, and guitarist Kim Jong-wan, lead guitarist Lee Jae-kyung, and bass guitarist Lee Jung-hoon. Since their formation in 1999, the four members remained intact until 2023, when drummer Jeong Jae-won left the group due to personal reasons.

The group name Nell was taken from the 1994 film of the same name. Nell first formed in 1999 after the four members failed to pass the college entrance exam. They began performing at local clubs and gained a following in the indie rock scene. They released two albums in 2001: their debut 'Reflection of' and their second album 'Speechless'. These albums sparked a revival of the emo-rock genre in South Korea. Their music spans various aspects of rock, from alternative to progressive, with Nell’s distinct sound that is easily recognizable to listeners.

In 2002, prominent musician Seo Taiji discovered the band. Soon after, Nell became the first group to be promoted under Goesoo Indigene, a subsidiary of the Seo Taiji Company. After four years, Nell parted ways with the label and signed with Woollim Entertainment in 2006.

Nell is inspired by British bands such as Radiohead, Muse, Coldplay, and Placebo. They are also close friends with industry peers Epik High, Dynamic Duo, Lovelyz, Pia, and Kim Sungkyu of INFINITE.

The band’s subsequent albums have all topped real-time charts. Nell’s third studio album, 'Healing Process', was recognized as one of the year's best recordings by Korean critics, and their fourth album, 'Separation Anxiety', ranked #1. Their fifth album, 'Slip Away', was released in 2012 after the members’ enlistment period.

Nell also performed at the second K-Pop Night Out at SXSW in Texas alongside other prominent K-pop artists. Their sixth album, 'Newton’s Apple', was ranked #2 on Billboard’s 10 Best K-Pop Albums of 2014. They have contributed multiple OST's as well as fellow artists' music, notably WANNA ONE's 'Forever and a Day', RM's 'Everything Goes' and G-Dragon's 'Today'.

On March 22, 2016, it was announced that Nell had ended their contract with Woollim Entertainment and established their independent record label, Space Bohemian. In August of that year, they released their first album under the company titled 'C'. Nell is widely considered to be one of the few bands in South Korea with a loyal core fandom, as seen in their multiple sold-out concerts. Their 2016 album C, which was barely promoted, topped the charts—further proof of the group’s impact.
